purpose: Compare actual same-request S2 optional NeuralRx and reserved conventional recovery against conventional-only, NRx-only, and eager dual execution while reclaiming slack for a separate MPS AI client.

fault_model.reason: exercise recovery and late-result fencing without substituting synthetic receiver compute

background.kind: separate MPS NeuralRx CUDA Graph client

policies.eager_dual: execute both actual receiver branches on every release
policies.s2_reserved: reserve NRx endpoint and a conventional recovery interval atomically; commit one result and reclaim the rest for background

interpretation_limit: Injected NRx invalidation validates recovery semantics and resource tradeoffs; channel-induced NRx/conventional utility differences require a separate SNR/channel trace experiment.
